_meta.scope: Decatur, Franklin, Perry, Pike, Wayne townships (Marion County). Citywide Indianapolis rental registry and citywide utilities are covered by a separate researcher; this file covers township-specific details and the included/excluded towns inside these townships.
_meta.fair_housing: Places, rules, services and infrastructure only. No demographics, schools, crime or resident descriptions were collected. Source pages that included that kind of content (e.g. the Perry Township Wikipedia page's list of high schools) were deliberately left out.

shared_sources.fact: Landlord-tenant small claims cases must be filed in the township small claims court where the property is located (Small Claims Rule 12); if the township has no court, they may be filed in any township. Lists all nine township court addresses.

AES Indiana tariff (effective July 27, 2026) lists Indianapolis, Beech Grove, Southport, Speedway, Clermont and Marion County among places where it provides electric service; the sheet says it is informational and not a full description of the territory.

Citizens Energy Group provides natural gas in the Indianapolis area, water in the 8-county Indianapolis area, and wastewater in Marion County. It sells water to communities that run their own water utilities (Speedway named) and has wastewater agreements with Ben Davis Conservancy District, City of Beech Grove and Tri-County Conservancy District, among others.
Citizens' Septic Tank Elimination Program (STEP) connects properties still on septic systems to sewer; owners can check a specific address with a Utility Availability Request.
Under Unigov, Beech Grove, Lawrence, Southport and Speedway are excluded cities/towns that keep most of their own government; Clermont and Homecroft are among the included towns.

decatur-township.jurisdiction: Decatur Township is the southwest-corner township of Marion County, governed as part of the consolidated City of Indianapolis. It has no included or excluded towns of its own; Camby (partly) and Valley Mills are unincorporated communities inside it.
decatur-township.local_rules_notes: No separate town-level rental rules apply, because no included or excluded town lies inside the township. Citywide Indianapolis/Marion County rules apply (covered separately).
decatur-township.eviction_court: Decatur Township Small Claims Court, 3730 S. Foltz St., Indianapolis, IN 46221, (317) 241-2854. Evictions on Decatur Township property must be filed here.

utilities.water: Citizens Energy Group in most of the township. Much of Decatur Township is still farmland, so some properties may be on private wells; check each address.
utilities.sewer: Citizens Energy Group in most of the township. Properties still on septic can check whether Citizens' STEP program covers them with a Utility Availability Request.

decatur-township.location: Southwest Marion County, with the White River forming its eastern line with Perry Township. I-465 and I-70 cross the northern part of the township, State Road 67 (Kentucky Avenue) runs through it, and the Ronald Reagan Parkway links the 1,500-acre AmeriPlex industrial park to I-70 near the airport. Indianapolis International Airport, about seven miles southwest of downtown, spans Decatur and Wayne townships and has its 2008 midfield terminal here; Southwestway Park (8400 Mann Road, along the White River) has trails and an 18-hole golf course.
unverified: Court ZIP code: the township's official court page says 46221, but the 2023 Warren Township brochure lists 3750 S. Foltz St., 46241. Use the official page (3730 / 46221), but confirm by phone before printing.
Exactly which parts of Decatur Township rely on private wells or septic. No source names specific areas; only that much of the township is still farmland.

Whether any part of Decatur Township is inside the Tri-County Conservancy District (a sewer district covering parts of Marion, Morgan and Hendricks counties and serving Heartland Crossing). Its pages don't say which Marion County areas it covers.
Southwestway Park acreage: Wikipedia gives both 587 and 487.5 acres. Leave the acreage out.
Which township the new I-69/I-465 interchange (opened August 2024, just west of the SR 37/Harding St interchange) sits in, Decatur or Perry. Not confirmed, so I-69 is left out of this text.
Straight-line distance from the township center to downtown is about 7.5 miles, but that figure is calculated from coordinates in red-door-city-facts-research.md, not taken from a source.

franklin-township.jurisdiction: Franklin Township is the southeast-corner township of Marion County, governed as part of the consolidated City of Indianapolis. The eastern portion of Beech Grove, an excluded city, lies inside it; Acton, Wanamaker and Gallaudet are unincorporated communities.
franklin-township.local_rules_notes: Outside Beech Grove, citywide Indianapolis/Marion County rules apply. Beech Grove is an excluded city with its own government and its own city-owned sewer utility. No Beech Grove rental registration or inspection ordinance could be found or confirmed.
franklin-township.eviction_court: Franklin Township Small Claims Court, 4531 Independence Square, Indianapolis, IN 46203, 317-784-1751. Evictions on Franklin Township property must be filed here.

utilities.water: Citizens Energy Group in most of the township. Franklin Township holds about 40% of Marion County's undeveloped farm ground, so rural properties may be on private wells; check each address.
utilities.sewer: Citizens Energy Group in most of the township, with septic likely on rural parcels (check through Citizens' Utility Availability Request). In Beech Grove, sewer is a city-owned utility that bills residents and pays Citizens for treatment.

franklin-township.location: Southeast side of Indianapolis, covering about 42 square miles. I-74 follows the old Michigan Road route (Southeastern Avenue) through the township, I-65 runs along its western edge, and Southport Road and Franklin Road are the main local corridors. Southeastway Park (5624 S. Carroll Rd., off I-74 at Acton Road) is a 188-acre nature park on Buck Creek, the township is home to the Marion County Fairgrounds, and suburban subdivisions sit next to working farmland.
unverified: Court address: a third-party directory (recordsfinder) gives 4351 Independence Square. The township's own courts page and the 2023 Warren Township brochure both say 4531, which is used here.

perry-township.jurisdiction: Perry Township is on the south side of Marion County, governed as part of the consolidated City of Indianapolis. It contains Southport (an excluded city), Homecroft (an included town) and the southwest third of Beech Grove (an excluded city).
perry-township.local_rules_notes: Southport's official city site lists no rental registration or landlord program; its Clerk-Treasurer handles building permits and trade licenses. Homecroft's ordinance list has nothing on rentals, and Indianapolis-Marion County law applies there as an included town. No Beech Grove rental ordinance could be confirmed.
perry-township.eviction_court: Perry Township Small Claims Court, 4925 Shelby Street, Suite 100, Indianapolis, IN 46227, (317) 786-9242. The court's own page says landlord-tenant cases 'shall be in the township where the real estate is located.'

utilities.water: Citizens Energy Group in most of the township.
utilities.sewer: Citizens Energy Group in most of the township. Beech Grove runs its own city-owned sewer utility and pays Citizens for treatment. Southport's sewer arrangement was not confirmed.
utilities.electric: AES Indiana, including Southport and Beech Grove.

perry-township.location: Directly south of Center Township and downtown, with the White River on its west side and Johnson County (Greenwood) to the south. I-65 and I-465 cross the township, and Madison Avenue, South Meridian Street (SR 135), US 31 and SR 37 are the main commuter roads. Landmarks include the University of Indianapolis, the historic Southport commercial district, and Perry Park (451 E. Stop 11 Rd.), home to Indy Parks' only indoor ice rink and a seasonal outdoor pool.

pike-township.jurisdiction: Pike Township is the northwest-corner township of Marion County, governed as part of the consolidated City of Indianapolis. Part of Clermont (an included town split between Pike and Wayne townships) lies inside it; Augusta and Traders Point are unincorporated communities.
pike-township.local_rules_notes: Clermont's own site says that as an included town, 'all laws of Indianapolis-Marion County now also apply in Clermont,' and its ordinance page lists no rental or landlord ordinance. Clermont is rewriting its town code (started 2023), so check the current code before relying on that.
pike-township.eviction_court: Pike Township Small Claims Court, 5665 Lafayette Road, Suite B, Indianapolis, IN 46254, 317-293-1842. Evictions on Pike Township property must be filed here.

utilities.sewer: Citizens Energy Group. Sewer construction in 1969 opened the township to development.

pike-township.location: Northwest side of Indianapolis, bordering Boone and Hamilton counties. I-65 and I-465 meet at the township's north junction, I-74 crosses its southwest corner (with no exits there), and Lafayette Road, Michigan Road, West 86th Street and Zionsville Road are the main corridors. Eagle Creek Park, about 5,000 acres including a 1,400-acre reservoir, is one of the largest municipal parks in the U.S.; other landmarks are Lafayette Square Mall (opened 1968), the Pyramids office buildings near Michigan Road and 86th Street, and the Park 100 business park.
unverified: No official Pike Township web page for the small claims court was found. The address comes from the 2023 Warren Township brochure (which leaves out the suite) and Indiana Legal Help's tenant-clinic listing (which gives Suite B).

Which half of Clermont lies in Pike: Wikipedia's Pike page says the 'northern half' in one place and 'a portion... in the southwest corner' in another, and its Wayne page says 'south half.' Safe wording: Clermont lies partly in Pike and partly in Wayne.
Clermont's water and sewer providers were not confirmed separately (assumed Citizens).

wayne-township.jurisdiction: Wayne Township is on the west side of Marion County, governed as part of the consolidated City of Indianapolis. It contains the town of Speedway (an excluded town with its own government) and the south part of Clermont (an included town).
wayne-township.local_rules_notes: Speedway requires a landlord license before an owner lets anyone occupy a rental unit, plus a rental unit permit for each unit, renewed every year. The license requires completing a landlord training program, and units can be inspected within 24 months of the permit. The town says the landlord license is valid until October 1 each year; short-term rentals need a separate $150 permit, valid one year and renewable at no charge (Speedway Municipal Code Ch. 5.48 and 5.49).
wayne-township.eviction_court: Wayne Township Small Claims Court, Wayne Township Government Center, 5401 W. Washington St., Indianapolis, IN 46241, (317) 241-9573. Evictions on Wayne Township property, including Speedway, must be filed here.

utilities.water: Citizens Energy Group in most of the township. Speedway runs its own water utility, billed by the Town Clerk-Treasurer, and buys some of its water from Citizens.
utilities.sewer: Citizens Energy Group in most of the township. Speedway runs its own wastewater utility. The Ben Davis Conservancy District owns the sewer lines in part of west-side Wayne Township and sends wastewater to Citizens for treatment.
utilities.electric: AES Indiana, including Speedway and Clermont.

wayne-township.location: West side of Indianapolis, between Center Township and Hendricks County. I-70, I-74 and I-465 run through the township, along with US 40 (Washington Street, the old National Road). Landmarks include the Indianapolis Motor Speedway in the town of Speedway (about six miles west of downtown, home of the Indianapolis 500 and Brickyard 400), the north half of Indianapolis International Airport with its FedEx hub, the Park Fletcher office park, and Krannert Park's recreation center (605 S. High School Rd., reopened January 2024 with a year-round indoor pool).
unverified: Speedway fees: the 2006 ordinance set a $20 application fee, a $125 license fee ($25 for owners of five or fewer units) and $15 per unit per year. Current fees were not confirmed and may have changed, since state law now limits local rental registration and inspection fees. Don't publish fee amounts without checking with the Speedway Clerk-Treasurer (317-246-4111).
Speedway Ordinance 1074 (amending the inspection and search-warrant language after a lawsuit) was seen only in search snippets; its page was not opened.
